notes: Your devices can now find each other, the floating dot is lighter on your machine, and Settings feels calmer.

changelog.headline: What's new in 1.0.15

sections.title: Ecosystem: your devices, one tree
items: Every machine running ELLA on your wifi can join a single tree, with one device as admin.

Pairing is a nine-digit code shown on the Ecosystem page. The admin types another device's code to add it straight away, or a device types the admin's code to ask to join. The code burns the moment it's used.
The admin names every device — Dad's PC, the studio laptop — and the tree shows on all of them, with who is admin and who is reachable right now.
Everything stays on your network. No account, no cloud, nobody in between. After pairing, the devices trust a key only they hold.
Controlling one device from another is coming next; this release is the connection.
Windows will ask once whether ELLA may talk on your private network. Say yes so your other devices can find this one.

sections.title: The floating dot, lighter
items: The dot now properly rests when you step away and wakes itself for an alarm — it no longer sits there burning battery and CPU for nothing.
Voice runs through one dedicated process instead of competing with everything else, so Windows can no longer throttle it mid-sentence.
Long replies no longer cut off partway through speaking.

sections.title: Settings, lighter
items: The whole Settings window has been redrawn flatter and quieter, and long lists — memory especially — now scroll smoothly instead of stuttering.
Small visual polish across notes, alarms and the games list.

changelog.data_safety: Your chats, memory, notes, portfolio and settings stay exactly as they are. Updates only replace the app's own program files. Nothing you have created is touched or deleted.
